'''Aleph-1''', also known as '''Hvedrungr''', is the [[Threnodian]] of [[Lahai-Roi]] and the main antagonist of [[Chapter III|Chapter III: To the Stars Yet to Shine]]. It is a [[Void Storm]] that erases people's existence and memories, unlike normal [[Tacet Discord]]s that just petrify them. It is considered the strongest Threnodian due to its existential erasure power, potentially linked to the region's focus on research and exploration of the world beyond Solaris-3, causing people to forget their origins. [[Denia]] is its Resonator.

Its appearance resembles that of a massive black hole, but with a blue iris flowing downwards as its center instead of an event horizon. Inside the center of its pupil is a tiny blue dot, and it has a white accretion disk. Aleph-1 seemingly has the same time dilation property as that of a blackhole, while Rover experienced less than one minute within its vicinity, days have passed in Solaris-3. 

It was formerly "sealed" behind the [[Stridergate|gateway]] by the [[Exostrider]]'s sword in [[Sundermere]].  

During ''[[The Star That Voyages Far]]'' it is revealed that Aleph-1 is alien to [[Solaris-3]], having come from beyond Solaris through the [[Stridergate]] alongside the Exostrider. 

During the events of ''[[All That Sunlight Touches]]'', [[Luuk Herssen]] revealed that 9 years prior, [[Schwarzloch]] attempted to weaken the Exostrider's seal on the Threnodian, causing [[Aemeath]] to seal it once more, at the cost of her life, thus condemning her to life as a digital ghost. By the events of [[Starlights from Yesterdays|''Starlights from Yesterdays'']], Aleph-1 has been banished to the furthest edges of the universe by the end of its battle against the Exostrider. [[Denia]] destroyed the final fragment of it remaining on Solaris-3 to ensure it had no connection to the planet by the end of [[Beneath a Melting Night Sky|''Beneath a Melting Night Sky'']].

== Abilities ==
Aleph-1 is deemed the strongest Threnodian due to its existential erasure power, being known as the Voidborn Threnodian due to its unique abilities to erase people's existence and memories, among other powers. [["The Shaper"|The Shaper]] states in [[Ode to the Second Sunrise|''Ode to the Second Sunrise'']] that it is the source of the Void Storms and all related phenomenon linked to it in spite of being sealed due its influence having affected numerous locations across Lahai-Roi through the substance known as Voidmatter, which spreads and gathers to form dangerous Waveworn Phenomenon when enough is gathered. While its main properties are erasure, Voidmatter can corrupt those such as the Exoswarm and humans into becoming Tacet Discords. According to Aemeath in [[The Star That Voyages Far|''The Star That Voyages Far'']], she confirms the theories that Aleph-1 is the devourer of existence and embodies voidance - the dissolution of all things. It is a living black hole with the properties of one such as time dilation, holding great power that she and [[Luuk Herssen]] claim that not just Lahai-Roi, but all of Solaris-3 would be consumed by Aleph-1 were it ever unsealed, as it had already done so towards other civilizations across the universe.

However, this power only primarily affects the living. Aemeath, who had entered the Threnodian, could verify its nature as she was dead since as no living soul can withstand the higher-dimension inside it. Though, she suggests during her attempts to head deeper to time-travel within the Threnodian that even a deceased digital ghost such as herself could have been erased eventually when she initiated a time loop. Lahai-Roi has also created many defenses to resist the Void Storms and Voidmatter the Threnodian unleashes, though upon nearly being unsealed, such defenses failed before its power.

Also, in spite of being a Threnodian that embodies erasure, during the battle between it and both the Rover and Exostrider in [[Starlights from Yesterdays|''Starlights from Yesterdays'']] Aleph-1 constructed a recreation of its own Exostrider as a controlled projection to fight the two by also enhancing it.

=== Void Storms ===
The Void Storm is a Waveworn Phenomenon that indiscriminately dissolves all matter and existence within its range, causing widespread devastation. While corrupting, its main ability is the erasure properties that causes the existence of others to be wiped away. Those who are consumed find themselves losing their very existence and are devoured, imprisoned in Voidspace where those across Solaris-3 lose memories of the ones lost to the Void Storms. While there are defenses against the Void Storms, they are a periodic threat that have caused many to vanish with the Exoswarm, becoming Tacet Discords. Certain individuals like [[Warren]] in [[Ode to the Second Sunrise|''Ode to the Second Sunrise'']] also found methods to create an artificial Void Storm.

''For the complete properties and abilities of the Void Storm, see [[Void Storm]].''

=== Voidspace ===
A higher-dimension in the depths of the Threnodian’s black hole, acting like a pitch-black kaleidoscope. Time and space do not flow, being tangled, where those devoured find themselves in a place where linear time is chaotic and are set to fade away eventually in due time while certain structures drift and exit the location randomly. The location is currently inaccessible to mankind at the moment, as with the exception of Aemeath, the living cannot survive the Voidmatter concentration that leads to it since any living entity entering this domain suffers a rapid loss of frequency, eventually leading to the total dissolution of their existence. 

''For the complete properties and abilities of the Voidspace, see [[Voidspace]].''

===Creations===
====Voidworms====
Extradimensional amalgamations of Exoswarm and Exostrider remains consumed and contaminated by Void Storms. As agents of Aleph-1, these beings share similar abilities through the Voidmatter Regulators on their headsd. Due to their similar threat level, the inhabitants of Lahai-Roi consider them as terrifying as the Void Storms due to being unpredictable natural disasters that devour everything in their path. So long as Aleph-1's influence remains, Voidworms that are destroyed can be brought back.

''For the complete properties and abilities of the Voidworm, see [[Voidworm]].''

=== Limitations ===
Upon its banishment from Solaris-3 in [[Starlights from Yesterdays|''Starlights from Yesterdays'']], Voidmatter across Lahai-Roi has now lowered and access to Voidspace is now impossible through normal methods. It was also confirmed in [[Beneath a Melting Night Sky|''Beneath a Melting Night Sky'']] that it needed a vessel to establish a connection and properly descend upon Solaris-3, which the [[Fractsidus]] knew and created in the form of Denia, who is MIA upon sending herself into Voidspace and having destroyed the final fragment of Aleph-1 residing in the region. While it could return to Solaris-3 once more, it will take time with no guarantee it could descend without a vessel that matches its nature as the void.

== Trivia ==
=== Etymology ===
* {{W|Aleph}} is the first letter of the {{W|Semitic abjads}}.
* {{W|Aleph numbers}} are a sequence of numbers used in mathematics, particularly {{W|set theory}}, to represent the size of {{W|infinite sets}}. Aleph-1 is the second smallest of these numbers, with the smallest being Aleph-0.
